lines: If I'd never noticed I was bad at it, or scared of it
Even I could've become friends with the ball

I bet I could've solved even Fermat's theorem
If Masaya, passing by, hadn't laughed at me
I'd have kept pedaling my bike with training wheels
Too weak, too clumsy—
if I didn't know it, I'd have saved the earth hey
That scribble I tore up and threw away
The haircut they said didn't suit me
That half-remembered, clumsy song
might've changed the world ey
To us, who were once geniuses
To you, who was once a prodigy

a shadow of what we were

Worry all you can worry; when the time comes, strike

We're late bloomers ey; when the time comes, strike

So what if it's a fate like fireworks
I feel I can see it through till this body of mine burns out ey

crossroads have I let slip past, I wonder
